chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Miskān, from Muḥammad al-Ḥalabī, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a woman performing tamattuʿ whose husband approached her before she had shortened [her hair]. So when she feared that he would overpower her, she reached toward the braids of her hair and clipped some of it with her teeth and cut it with her nails. Is there anything upon her? He عليه السلام said: No. Not everyone finds scissors.

key_terms.تُقَصِّرَ: to shorten the hair as part of exiting iḥram
key_terms.قُرُونِهَا: the braids or locks of her hair

ai.seo_question: If a woman in tamattuʿ cuts her hair with her teeth or nails before taqsir, does anything become due upon her?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a woman in ḥajj al-tamattuʿ who needed to exit iḥram by shortening her hair before her husband could lawfully approach her. The Imam عليه السلام rules that trimming the hair with teeth or nails suffices in such a case, indicating practical allowance when scissors are unavailable.
